mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the discount rate applied to future equity cash flows, lowering the present value of expected dividends and earnings, which drives S&P 500 forward returns negative over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for at least 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the high-rate period (p > 0.10 in t-test), or the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS does not exceed 5.25% for 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a strengthening labor market, which raises consumer confidence and corporate earnings expectations, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 10% month-over-month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.5 percentage points in the same month
failure_condition: The 60-day forward return is negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger, or the correlation between PAYEMS/UNRATE change and SPX 60d return is <0.3 in out-of-sample tests.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures ( proxy via GDPC1 ) exceeding 2% suggests growing consumer demand, which elevates earnings expectations and supports equity valuations, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10), or GDPC1 growth decelerates below 1% in the following month.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 5% in two consecutive months indicates weakening supply-side constraints, prompting firms to raise prices and invest in productivity, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by >5% in two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative despite the supply contraction, or the effect persists for <1 month before reversing.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly inflation rate (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months while the Federal Funds rate remains near zero, the market anticipates persistent price pressures, causing equity valuations to adjust downward and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for 2 months with FEDFUNDS < 0.25%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or inflation decelerates without a corresponding equity sell-off.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in job openings (proxy via HOUST) coupled with a decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) creates labor market tightness that boosts consumer spending and corporate investment, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST increases by at least 15% in a month while UNRATE falls by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is flat or negative despite the labor indicators meeting the trigger, or the interaction effect is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of persistent monetary easing (FEDFUNDS < 4%), the 10-day rolling average of S&P 500 volatility declines, indicating reduced uncertainty and allowing risk premiums to compress, which produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.10) during the easing regime, or volatility does not fall as expected.

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in retail sales ( proxy via GDPC1 ) of 4% or more suggests weakening demand, which raises the cost of capital for growth-oriented firms and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 decreases by at least 4% in three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10), or retail sales recover in the following quarter.
